verdicts.reason: A sets the body copy on one clean line and centres the stack well, but the tracked attribution 'PACEWELL, THE PATIENT COACH' is now almost as wide and heavy as the headline, so the fine print competes with the message. B keeps the hierarchy right but leaves the orphan 'next.', and its small text cluster sits in a lot of empty yellow, so it reads like a shrunk copy.

In A the body line runs nearly edge to edge with tiny side margins, the oversized attribution competes with the headline, and the stack sits high, leaving dead space at the bottom. B is centred and the hierarchy is right, but it keeps the orphan 'next.', and its small type underuses the banner.

A is a centred, balanced stack with correct hierarchy; its only flaws are the orphan 'next.' and small, timid type. B pushes the centred text block off to the left with no grid logic, leaving a large empty strip on the right, and it keeps the same orphan, so it looks accidental.
